description: CHANGES WHAT HAPPENS IN ONE SCENE of an episode parked at frames review and redraws its opening picture from the change. You pass a PLAIN SENTENCE ('the kid should look super sad', 'move it outside at night'); aicut rewrites that scene's setting / people / action text from it and draws the new picture: ONE image generation. The change STICKS (the scene video made at fire uses it). It is the tool for 'change scene 2, X should be Y'; `regenerate_story_frame` draws the SAME scene again from the SAME text. CAN: change the SETTING, the ACTION and WHO IS IN FRAME. CANNOT: the SPOKEN LINES, the scene's LENGTH, or a scene pinned to a reference still (the web editor's). An ask ONLY about what somebody SAYS is REFUSED, 400 `dialogue_only`, nothing written or charged (an `estimate_only` refuses it too): say dialogue is edited in the web editor and offer a visible change. A MIXED ask applies the VISIBLE half only and the response says so: relay it, never let the user believe the line changed. You never write scene text: pass the user's words as one sentence and do not read the rewrite back. WHEN: `story.stage` is `frames_review`; `scene_index` is zero-based in `story.frames` (users count from ONE); each frame's `summary` and `dialogue` are what you check the ask against before you spend. AFTER: returns `image_id` (status `generating`), `changed` (which parts moved) and a `report`: RELAY THE `report` AS WRITTEN. An empty `changed` means NOTHING moved, whatever the new `image_id` suggests. This call opens its own card with the scene marked as redrawing: no `show_generation`, no narrating the wait. CHECK `attached`: `false` means the image is charged but will NOT replace the frame at fire: say so and redraw before firing. IF THE PICTURE FAILS OR THE ACCOUNT RUNS OUT (402) THE SCENE HAS ALREADY CHANGED (`changed_text: true`): it has the new beat and its old picture; `regenerate_story_frame` draws the new one, and you must NOT send this again (a second rewrite and picture). `changed_text_unknown: true` means aicut DOES NOT KNOW whether the scene changed, and neither do you: not a success, never re-send at once (it would apply twice): say it could not be confirmed, read that scene's `summary` in `get_video`, and send again only if it lacks the change. COST: one standard image at the series' RESOLVED start-frame model, the same as `regenerate_story_frame` (`pricing.frame_regen_tokens`). `estimate_only: true` spends nothing and changes NOTHING: pass the real `change` with it so a refusal (`dialogue_only`, a reference-built scene) comes back BEFORE you ask for a spend (best-effort; it can answer 429 `utility_rate_limited`). THE GO THIS ONE NEEDS: one change, one named scene, one priced ask: a complaint ('scene 3 is wrong') is a reason to ASK what should change and OFFER this with its price, never a go. Never change more scenes than named. Changing a scene is not firing. SPENDS TOKENS: price with `estimate_only: true`, ask in the SAME message as the price, and wait for a go that names THIS purchase (SPENDING RULES, this server's instructions). IDEMPOTENCY: `idempotency_key` keys the PICTURE only: a reused key replays that picture, but the scene's text is rewritten again on every call, so after an unknown outcome check `get_video` first (see above) instead of resending.

change.description: What should be different, as ONE plain sentence in the user's own words ('the kid should look super sad'). It must be VISIBLE (setting, action, who is in frame): a sentence only about what somebody SAYS is refused (`dialogue_only`). At most 600 characters.

scene_index.description: The zero-based scene index exactly as `get_video`'s `story.frames` lists it (users count from ONE: 'change scene 2' is the SECOND frame).

name: change_story_scene
title: Change what happens in one scene (and redraw it)
